features.quote: Pterodactylus was a small pterosaur compared to other famous genera such as Pteranodon and Quetzalcoatlus, and it also lived earlier, during the Late Jurassic period, while both Pteranodon and Quetzalcoatlus lived during the Late Cretaceous.

features.claim: Its wings were made of a skin and muscle membrane stretching from its long fourth finger to its hind limbs.
features.quote: Like all pterosaurs, Pterodactylus had wings formed by a skin and muscle membrane stretching from its elongated fourth finger to its hind limbs.

features.claim: The skulls of adult Pterodactylus were long and thin.
features.quote: The skulls of adult Pterodactylus were long and thin, with about 90 narrow and conical teeth.

features.claim: It had about 90 narrow, conical teeth.
features.quote: The skulls of adult Pterodactylus were long and thin, with about 90 narrow and conical teeth.

features.claim: The teeth went back from the tips of both jaws and got smaller farther from the jaw tips.
features.quote: The teeth extended back from the tips of both jaws, and became smaller farther away from the jaw tips.

features.claim: The skull and jaws were straight.
features.quote: Another autapomorphy that Pterodactylus has is that the skull and jaws were straight, which are unlike the upwardly curved jaws seen in the related ctenochasmatids.

features.claim: It had a crest on its skull made mainly of soft tissues.
features.quote: Pterodactylus, like related pterosaurs, had a crest on its skull composed mainly of soft tissues.

features.claim: In adult Pterodactylus, the crest extended between the back edge of the antorbital fenestra and the back of the skull.
features.quote: In adult Pterodactylus, this crest extended between the back edge of the antorbital fenestra and the back of the skull.

features.claim: In at least one specimen, the crest had a short bony base.
features.quote: In at least one specimen, the crest had a short bony base, also seen in related pterosaurs like Germanodactylus.

features.claim: Solid crests have only been found on large, fully adult specimens of Pterodactylus.
features.quote: Solid crests have only been found on large, fully adult specimens of Pterodactylus, indicating that this was a display structure that became larger and more well developed as individuals reached maturity.

features.claim: Pterodactylus antiquus had an estimated adult wingspan of about 1.04 meters.
features.quote: Pterodactylus antiquus was a relatively small pterosaur, with an estimated adult wingspan of about 1.04 meters (3 ft 5 in), based on the only known adult specimen, which is represented by an isolated skull.

not_this.claim: Older pictures that show Pterodactylus as a bat-like animal with fur are wrong.
not_this.quote: Sömmerring did not change his opinion that these forms were bats and this "bat model" for interpreting pterosaurs would remain influential long after a consensus had been reached around 1860 that they were reptiles.

not_this.claim: Older pictures that show Pterodactylus as an aquatic animal using its wings as flippers are wrong.
not_this.quote: The idea that pterosaurs were aquatic animals persisted among a minority of scientists as late as 1830, when the German zoologist Johann Georg Wagler published a text on "amphibians" which included an illustration of Pterodactylus using its wings as flippers.

not_this.claim: Older pictures that show Pterodactylus as a shore bird are wrong.
not_this.quote: He also refuted a hypothesis by Johann Friedrich Blumenbach that it would have been a shore bird.

debated.claim: It is uncertain whether the soft tissue crest of Pterodactylus extended backward behind the skull.
debated.quote: In 2013, pterosaur researcher S. Christopher Bennett noted that other authors claimed that the soft tissue crest of Pterodactylus extended backward behind the skull; Bennett himself, however, didn't find any evidence for the crest extending past the back of the skull.

debated.claim: It is uncertain whether Pterodactylus had a bony cranial crest.
debated.quote: Studies of Pterodactylus, however, conclude that it may even lack a bony cranial crest, though several analysis have proven that Pterodactylus may in fact have a crest made up of soft tissue instead of bone.

second_reading.claim: The wing membrane was supported inside by collagen fibres and outside by keratinous ridges.
second_reading.quote: It was supported internally by collagen fibres and externally by keratinous ridges.

second_reading.quote: Most of these specimens have been reclassified in the related species Aerodactylus scolopaciceps, which may however be nothing more than a junior synonym.
